title: When the grid fails
alt: A face-on section from the street to the data hall. On a normal day the grid feeds the racks through the switchgear and the UPS. The grid fails: the street cable goes grey, a break mark appears at the street vault with the label Grid power lost, and the lights flicker while the racks stay on. The batteries feed the racks through the UPS. The standby generator in the yard starts, with exhaust and noise; the switchgear hands the load to it; the UPS recharges the batteries; when the grid is back the switchgear hands back and the generator stops.

steps.caption: On a normal day the grid feeds the racks through the switchgear and the UPS. The batteries stay charged, and the standby generator waits in the yard.
The grid fails. The cable from the street goes dead. The lights flicker, but the racks stay on.
The batteries take over at once. Through the UPS they carry the racks with no break, for 10 to 15 minutes if needed.
The standby generator starts in the yard. It is ready to take the load in about 10 to 20 seconds.
The switchgear hands the load to the generator. Its power now runs through the UPS to the racks.
The UPS recharges the batteries from the generator.
When the grid is back, the switchgear hands back to it, and the generator stops.
